Re-install the serve engine via\n\u003cstrong\u003eCookbook → Dependencies\u003c/strong\u003e to get a CUDA-enabled build.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe same split applies to AMD/ROCm: seeing \u003ccode\u003e/dev/kfd\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e/dev/dri\u003c/code\u003e inside\nthe container confirms device passthrough, not ROCm userspace or a\nROCm-enabled vLLM/llama.cpp build. \u003ccode\u003erocm-smi\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003erocminfo\u003c/code\u003e are not expected\ninside the slim Odysseus image.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOllama with Docker.\u003c/strong\u003e If Ollama runs on the host, add this endpoint in\nSettings:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1\"\u003e\u003cpre lang=\"text\" class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehttp://host.docker.internal:11434/v1\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOllama must listen outside its own loopback interface:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" dir=\"auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama serve\"\u003e\u003cpre\u003eOLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama serve\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis connects Odysseus in Docker to an Ollama server that is already running on\nyour host machine; it does not start Ollama inside the container.\n\u003ccode\u003ehost.docker.internal\u003c/code\u003e is Docker's hostname for the host machine from inside the\ncontainer. See \u003ca href=\"/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus/blob/main/docs/email-outlook.md\"\u003edocs/email-outlook.md\u003c/a\u003e for the\ncurrent limitation and the planned integration direction.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eSecurity Notes\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-security-notes\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Security Notes\" href=\"#security-notes\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOdysseus is a self-hosted workspace with powerful local tools: shell access, file uploads, model downloads, web research, email/calendar integrations, and API tokens. Treat it like an admin console.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep \u003ccode\u003eAUTH_ENABLED=true\u003c/code\u003e for any network-accessible deployment.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep \u003ccode\u003eLOCALHOST_BYPASS=false\u003c/code\u003e outside local development.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUse \u003ccode\u003eSECURE_COOKIES=true\u003c/code\u003e when Odysseus is served through HTTPS by a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eDo not expose it directly to the public internet without HTTPS and a trusted reverse proxy or private access layer.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edata/\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elogs/\u003c/code\u003e, databases, uploads, generated media, backups, auth/session files, API keys, and model/provider tokens out of Git and private shares. They are ignored by default.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eReview \u003ccode\u003edata/auth.json\u003c/code\u003e after first boot: disable open signup unless you intentionally want it, make only your own account admin, and keep demo/test accounts non-admin.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eNon-admin users do not get shell/Python/file read/write by default, and admin-only routes/tools such as MCP management, API tokens, webhooks, model/cookbook serving, backup/vault, and app settings are admin-gated. Other features are controlled by per-user privileges, so review each user's privileges before exposing a deployment.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRotate any API keys or tokens that were ever pasted into a shared chat, demo, screenshot, or log.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eIf you enable API tokens or webhooks, create separate tokens per integration and delete unused ones.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ePrefer binding manual development runs to \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1\u003c/code\u003e; bind to \u003ccode\u003e0.0.0.0\u003c/code\u003e only when you intentionally want LAN/reverse-proxy access.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep ChromaDB, SearXNG, ntfy, Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, databases, and raw model/provider APIs internal-only. Expose only the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint through your trusted proxy or private access layer.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBefore publishing a fork, run \u003ccode\u003egit status --short\u003c/code\u003e and confirm no private files from \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003edata/\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003elogs/\u003c/code\u003e, uploads, backups, or local databases are staged.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003ePrivate or proxied deployments\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-private-or-proxied-deployments\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Private or proxied deployments\" href=\"#private-or-proxied-deployments\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOdysseus serves plain HTTP on its app port. Docker Compose binds Odysseus and the bundled services to \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1\u003c/code\u003e by default, so a typical production/private setup is:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep Odysseus on localhost, for example \u003ccode\u003e127.0.0.1:7000\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eTerminate HTTPS at a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ePut the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint behind that layer.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eKeep raw service and model ports internal-only.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCloudflare Access, Tailscale, Caddy, nginx, and Traefik can all fit this pattern; none are required by Odysseus. Odysseus","","\u003e **Branch note:** `dev` is the default branch and contains the latest development changes, but it may be unstable. For the more stable curated branch, use [`main`](https://github.com/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus/tree/main).","","```","───────────────────────────────────────────────"," ⊹ ࣪ ˖ ૮( ˶ᵔ ᵕ ᵔ˶ )っ  Odysseus vers. 1.0","───────────────────────────────────────────────","```","","![Odysseus](docs/odysseus.jpg)","","A self-hosted AI workspace -- meant to be the self-hosted version of the UI experience you get from ChatGPT and Claude. But with more jank and fun. Running on your own hardware, with your own data -- local-first, privacy-first, and no trojan.","","## Features","  - **Chat** -- chat with any local model or API; adding them is super simple.\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003evLLM · llama.cpp · Ollama · OpenRouter · OpenAI · GitHub Copilot\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Agent** -- hand it tools and let it run the whole task itself.\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003ebuilt on [opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) · MCP · web · files · shell · skills · memory\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Cookbook** -- Scans your hardware, recommends models, click to download and serve.. easy!\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003ebuilt on [llmfit](https://github.com/AlexsJones/llmfit) · VRAM-aware · GGUF / FP8 / AWQ · fit scoring · vLLM / llama.cpp serving\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Deep Research** -- multi-step runs that gather, read, and synthesize sources into a nice visual report.\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003eadapted from [Tongyi DeepResearch](https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/DeepResearch)\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Compare** -- a fun tool to compare models side by side. Test completely blind, no bias!\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003emulti-model · blind test · synthesis\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Documents** -- YOU write the text, AI is there to assist, not the opposite.\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003emulti-tab editor · markdown · HTML · CSV · syntax highlighting · AI edits · suggestions\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Memory / Skills** -- Persistent memory and skills, your agent evolves over time as it better understands you and your tasks!\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003eChromaDB · fastembed (ONNX) · vector + keyword retrieval · import/export\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Email** -- IMAP/SMTP inbox with AI triage built in: urgency reminders, auto-tag, auto-summary, auto-reply drafts, auto-spam.\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003eIMAP · SMTP · per-account routing · CalDAV-aware\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Notes \u0026 Tasks** -- Quick notes with reminders, a todo list, and scheduled tasks the agent can act on.\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003enote pings · checklist · cron-style tasks · ntfy / browser / email channels\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Calendar** -- Local-first calendar with CalDAV sync to Radicale / Nextcloud / Apple / Fastmail.\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003eCalDAV pull · .ics import/export · per-calendar colors · agent-aware\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Works on mobile** -- looks and runs great on your phone, not just desktop.\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003eresponsive · installable (PWA) · touch gestures\u003c/sub\u003e","  - **Extras** -- more to explore, happy if you give it a go!\u003cbr\u003e　\u003csub\u003eimage editor · theme editor · file uploads (vision + PDF) · web search · presets · sessions · 2FA\u003c/sub\u003e","","## Demo","A full, hover-to-play tour lives on the landing page (`docs/index.html`).","","\u003cdetails\u003e","\u003csummary\u003eScreenshots / clips\u003c/summary\u003e","","### Chat \u0026 Agents","![Chat \u0026 Agents](docs/chat.gif)","### Deep Research","![Deep Research](docs/research.gif)","### Compare","![Compare](docs/compare.gif)","### Documents","![Documents](docs/document.gif)","### Notes \u0026 Tasks","![Notes \u0026 Tasks](docs/notes.gif)","","\u003c/details\u003e","","## Quick Start","","Defaults work out of the box: clone, run, then configure models/search/email","inside **Settings**. Only edit `.env` for deployment-level overrides like","`APP_BIND`, `APP_PORT`, `AUTH_ENABLED`, `DATABASE_URL`, or a pre-seeded admin password.","","On first setup, Odysseus creates an admin account (`admin` unless","`ODYSSEUS_ADMIN_USER` is set) and prints a temporary password in the terminal.","For Docker installs, the same line is in `docker compose logs odysseus`.","Use that for the first login, then change it in **Settings**.","","Contributing? See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup, testing, and","pull request guidelines.","","### Docker (recommended)","```bash","git clone https://github.com/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus.git","cd odysseus","cp .env.example .env       # optional, but recommended for explicit defaults","docker compose up -d --build","```","To include optional extras in the image (PDF viewer, Office extraction; includes AGPL PyMuPDF), build with `docker compose build --build-arg INSTALL_OPTIONAL=true` before `up`.","","Open `http://localhost:7000` when the containers are healthy. Docker Compose","binds the web UI to `127.0.0.1` by default. If the port is taken, set","`APP_PORT=7001` in `.env` and recreate the container. Set `APP_BIND=0.0.0.0`","only when you intentionally want LAN/reverse-proxy access.","","### Native Linux / macOS","```bash","git clone https://github.com/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus.git","cd odysseus","python3 -m venv venv","source venv/bin/activate","pip install -r requirements.txt","python setup.py","python -m uvicorn app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7000","```","Requirements: Python 3.11+. Cookbook also needs `tmux` for background model","downloads and serves. The app itself is lightweight; local model serving is the","heavy part and depends on the model, runtime, GPU, and VRAM, so small hosts can","connect to API or remote model servers instead. Use `--host 0.0.0.0` only when you intentionally want LAN/reverse-proxy access.","","### Apple Silicon","Docker on macOS cannot use the Metal GPU. For GPU-accelerated Cookbook on an","M-series Mac, run Odysseus natively:","","```bash","git clone https://github.com/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus.git","cd odysseus","./start-macos.sh","```","","It launches at `http://127.0.0.1:7860`. To expose it to your phone over a trusted LAN/VPN such as Tailscale, bind all interfaces:","","```bash","ODYSSEUS_HOST=0.0.0.0 ./start-macos.sh","# then open http://\u003ctailscale-ip\u003e:7860","```","","The script also reads `.env` at startup, so `APP_BIND=0.0.0.0` and `APP_PORT`","set there are picked up automatically without a command-line override each run.","","Keep `AUTH_ENABLED=true` (the default) before binding outside loopback. Do not","expose this port directly to the public internet. To build a clickable app wrapper:","","```bash","./build-macos-app.sh","```","","\u003cdetails\u003e","\u003csummary\u003eCookbook, GPU, Ollama, and troubleshooting notes\u003c/summary\u003e","","**Docker bundled services.** Compose starts Odysseus, ChromaDB, SearXNG, and","ntfy. Odysseus and the bundled service ports bind to `127.0.0.1` by default, so","they are reachable from the host but not exposed to your LAN/public internet","unless you opt in.","","**Cookbook storage in Docker.** Downloads live in `./data/huggingface`","(`~/.cache/huggingface` in the container). Cookbook-installed Python CLIs and","serve engines live in `./data/local` (`~/.local` in the container), so they","survive container recreation.","","**Remote servers.** In **Cookbook -\u003e Settings -\u003e Servers**, generate the","Odysseus SSH key and add the public key to the remote server's","`~/.ssh/authorized_keys`. From the host you can also run:","","```bash","ssh-copy-id -i data/ssh/id_ed25519.pub user@server","```","","**Docker GPU overlays.** CPU-only users can skip this section. Cookbook can","only detect GPUs that Docker exposes to the container — if the host runtime or","device passthrough is not configured, Cookbook sees the iGPU, another card, or","CPU instead of your intended GPU.","","For NVIDIA, `scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh` diagnoses GPU passthrough and can","optionally install the host runtime or update `.env`.","","```bash","# Read-only diagnostic (default — installs nothing, never edits .env):","scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh","","# Print OS-specific install commands without running them:","scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh --print-install-commands","","# Install NVIDIA Container Toolkit on Ubuntu/Debian (requires sudo):","scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh --install-nvidia-toolkit","","# Write COMPOSE_FILE to .env (only when GPU passthrough is confirmed working):","scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh --enable-nvidia-overlay","","# Full assisted setup — install toolkit, then enable overlay if passthrough works:","scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh --install-nvidia-toolkit --enable-nvidia-overlay","```","","Safety notes:","- The app never installs host GPU runtime automatically.","- The app never edits `.env` automatically.","- `.env` is only modified when `--enable-nvidia-overlay` is explicitly passed,","  and only after GPU passthrough succeeds. `--yes` skips prompts but does not","  bypass the passthrough gate.","- `.env.bak.*` backups created by `--enable-nvidia-overlay` are ignored by","  Git and the Docker build context.","","To enable manually without the script, add this to `.env`:","","```bash","COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:docker/gpu.nvidia.yml","```","","**AMD / ROCm.** AMD setup is read-only diagnostic plus manual `.env` edit. Run:","","```bash","scripts/check-docker-amd-gpu.sh","```","","Then add the reported values to `.env`, replacing `RENDER_GID` with your host's","numeric render group id:","","```bash","COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:docker/gpu.amd.yml","RENDER_GID=989","```","","For NVIDIA/AMD GPU support, also read the comments in the selected overlay file: docker/gpu.nvidia.yml or docker/gpu.amd.yml.","","**Stack-management UIs (Portainer, Coolify, Dockhand, etc.).** These tools","often accept only a single Compose file and do not reliably honor `COMPOSE_FILE`","or multiple `-f` overlays. CLI users should keep using the `COMPOSE_FILE`","overlay workflow above. For stack UIs, point the stack at one of the standalone","files instead, which bundle the base stack plus the GPU settings:","","- `docker-compose.gpu-nvidia.yml` — still requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit","  on the host.","- `docker-compose.gpu-amd.yml` — still requires host ROCm/kfd/DRI setup, the","  `video`/`render` group membership, and `RENDER_GID` when needed.","","The base `docker-compose.yml` plus the `docker/gpu.*.yml` overlays remain the","source of truth; the standalone files mirror them for single-file deployments.","","Verify after enabling either overlay:","","```bash","docker compose exec odysseus nvidia-smi -L   # NVIDIA","docker compose exec odysseus sh -lc 'test -e /dev/kfd \u0026\u0026 test -d /dev/dri \u0026\u0026 ls -l /dev/kfd /dev/dri/renderD*'  # AMD","```","","\u003e **GPU passthrough ≠ llama.cpp CUDA.** `nvidia-smi` passing inside the","\u003e container confirms Docker GPU access, but llama.cpp also needs `cudart` and","\u003e the CUDA Toolkit at runtime. If Cookbook logs show `Unable to find cudart","\u003e library`, `Could NOT find CUDAToolkit`, `CUDA Toolkit not found`, or","\u003e tensors/layers assigned to CPU, that is a Cookbook/llama.cpp build issue —","\u003e not a Docker passthrough failure. Re-install the serve engine via","\u003e **Cookbook → Dependencies** to get a CUDA-enabled build.","\u003e","\u003e The same split applies to AMD/ROCm: seeing `/dev/kfd` and `/dev/dri` inside","\u003e the container confirms device passthrough, not ROCm userspace or a","\u003e ROCm-enabled vLLM/llama.cpp build. `rocm-smi` and `rocminfo` are not expected","\u003e inside the slim Odysseus image.","","**Ollama with Docker.** If Ollama runs on the host, add this endpoint in","Settings:","","```text","http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1","```","","Ollama must listen outside its own loopback interface:","","```bash","OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:11434 ollama serve","```","","This connects Odysseus in Docker to an Ollama server that is already running on","your host machine; it does not start Ollama inside the container.","`host.docker.internal` is Docker's hostname for the host machine from inside the","container. Cookbook **Serve** is a separate workflow for serving downloaded","models through Odysseus/llama.cpp, so Windows users with an existing Ollama","install usually only need to add the endpoint in Settings.","","**Useful checks.**","","```bash","docker compose ps","docker compose logs --tail=120 odysseus","docker compose logs odysseus | grep -E 'ChromaDB|MemoryVectorStore|DEGRADED'","```","","**macOS details.** `start-macos.sh` installs Homebrew deps, creates the venv,","runs setup, and starts uvicorn on port `7860` because AirPlay often holds","`7000`. It uses llama.cpp/Ollama for Metal. vLLM/SGLang are CUDA/ROCm-only and","do not run on macOS. MLX-only models are not served by Odysseus.","","\u003c/details\u003e","","### Native Windows","","**One-command launcher** (creates the venv, installs deps, runs setup, starts the","server; safe to re-run):","","```powershell","git clone https://github.com/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus.git","cd odysseus","powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\\launch-windows.ps1","```","","Or do it by hand:","","```powershell","git clone https://github.com/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus.git","cd odysseus","py -3.11 -m venv venv","venv\\Scripts\\Activate.ps1","pip install -r requirements.txt","python setup.py","python -m uvicorn app:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 7000","```","","If `python` points at an older interpreter, use `py -3.12` (or another installed","3.11+ version) for the venv step.","","**Requirements:** Python 3.11+. The core app (chat, agent, memory, documents,","email, calendar, deep research) runs fully native. For full **Cookbook** background","model downloads and the agent shell tool, also install","[Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) (provides `bash.exe`).","Local GPU *serving* of vLLM/SGLang needs Linux/WSL2; for a local model on Windows,","[Ollama](https://ollama.com/download) is the easiest path — point Odysseus at","`http://localhost:11434/v1` in Settings.","","Open `http://localhost:7000`, log in with the generated admin password,","and configure everything else inside **Settings**.","","## Troubleshooting \u0026 Advanced Setup","","### `chromadb-client` conflicts with embedded ChromaDB","If `chromadb-client` (the lightweight HTTP-only package) is installed alongside the full `chromadb` package, Odysseus starts but ChromaDB silently falls back to HTTP-only mode and fails.","","**Fix:** uninstall `chromadb-client` and force-reinstall the full package:","```bash","./venv/bin/pip uninstall chromadb-client -y","./venv/bin/pip install --force-reinstall chromadb","```","","### HTTPS + LAN/Tailscale exposure","To expose Odysseus on a local network or Tailscale with HTTPS:","1. Change the bind address to `0.0.0.0` in `.env` (`APP_BIND=0.0.0.0` or `ODYSSEUS_HOST=0.0.0.0`).","2. Generate a locally-trusted cert for your LAN/Tailscale IPs using [mkcert](https://github.com/FiloSottile/mkcert):","   ```bash","   mkcert -install","   mkcert -cert-file cert.pem -key-file key.pem 192.168.1.100 tailscale-ip","   ```","3. Run `uvicorn` with the generated certs:","   ```bash","   python -m uvicorn app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 7000 --ssl-certfile=cert.pem --ssl-keyfile=key.pem","   ```","4. Install the `mkcert` CA on any other device you want to access Odysseus from (e.g., for iOS, email the `rootCA.pem` to yourself, install the profile, and trust it in Certificate Trust Settings).","","### Optional Dependencies","`requirements-optional.txt` contains packages that unlock extra features. It is not installed by default.","","| Package | Feature unlocked |","|---------|-----------------|","| `faster-whisper` | Local speech-to-text (microphone -\u003e text) via the \"local\" STT provider. |","| `duckduckgo-search` | DuckDuckGo as a search provider option. |","| `PyMuPDF` | PDF page rendering in the side viewer panel and form-filling. (Note: AGPL-3.0) |","| `markitdown` | Office/EPUB document text extraction (converts .docx/.xlsx/.pptx/.xls/.epub to Markdown). |","","### Outlook / Office 365 email","Odysseus email accounts currently use IMAP/SMTP username-password auth. Outlook","and Microsoft 365 generally require OAuth instead, so normal Microsoft mailbox","passwords will fail. See [docs/email-outlook.md](docs/email-outlook.md) for the","current limitation and the planned integration direction.","","## Security Notes","Odysseus is a self-hosted workspace with powerful local tools: shell access, file uploads, model downloads, web research, email/calendar integrations, and API tokens. Treat it like an admin console.","","- Keep `AUTH_ENABLED=true` for any network-accessible deployment.","- Keep `LOCALHOST_BYPASS=false` outside local development.","- Use `SECURE_COOKIES=true` when Odysseus is served through HTTPS by a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.","- Do not expose it directly to the public internet without HTTPS and a trusted reverse proxy or private access layer.","- Keep `.env`, `data/`, `logs/`, databases, uploads, generated media, backups, auth/session files, API keys, and model/provider tokens out of Git and private shares. They are ignored by default.","- Review `data/auth.json` after first boot: disable open signup unless you intentionally want it, make only your own account admin, and keep demo/test accounts non-admin.","- Non-admin users do not get shell/Python/file read/write by default, and admin-only routes/tools such as MCP management, API tokens, webhooks, model/cookbook serving, backup/vault, and app settings are admin-gated. Other features are controlled by per-user privileges, so review each user's privileges before exposing a deployment.","- Rotate any API keys or tokens that were ever pasted into a shared chat, demo, screenshot, or log.","- If you enable API tokens or webhooks, create separate tokens per integration and delete unused ones.","- Prefer binding manual development runs to `127.0.0.1`; bind to `0.0.0.0` only when you intentionally want LAN/reverse-proxy access.","- Keep ChromaDB, SearXNG, ntfy, Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, databases, and raw model/provider APIs internal-only. Expose only the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint through your trusted proxy or private access layer.","- Before publishing a fork, run `git status --short` and confirm no private files from `.env`, `data/`, `logs/`, uploads, backups, or local databases are staged.","","### Private or proxied deployments","Odysseus serves plain HTTP on its app port. Docker Compose binds Odysseus and the bundled services to `127.0.0.1` by default, so a typical production/private setup is:","","1. Keep Odysseus on localhost, for example `127.0.0.1:7000`.","2. Terminate HTTPS at a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.","3. Put the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint behind that layer.","4. Keep raw service and model ports internal-only.","","Cloudflare Access, Tailscale, Caddy, nginx, and Traefik can all fit this pattern; none are required by Odysseus. If your access layer reaches Odysseus on the same host, proxy to `http://127.0.0.1:7000` and keep `AUTH_ENABLED=true`, `LOCALHOST_BYPASS=false`, and `SECURE_COOKIES=true`.","","Common internal-only ports from the default docs/compose setup:","","| Port | Service |","|---|---|","| `7000` | Odysseus raw app port |","| `8080` | SearXNG |","| `8091` | ntfy |","| `8100` | ChromaDB host port for manual/compose access |","| `11434` | Ollama |","| `8000-8020` | Common local model/provider APIs |","","## Contributing","Help is welcome. <p dir="auto">A self-hosted AI workspace -- meant to be the self-hosted version of the UI experience you get from ChatGPT and Claude. But with more jank and fun. Running on your own hardware, with your own data -- local-first, privacy-first, and no trojan.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Features</h2><a id="user-content-features" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Features" href="#features"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Chat</strong> -- chat with any local model or API; adding them is super simple.<br>　<sub>vLLM · llama.cpp · Ollama · OpenRouter · OpenAI · GitHub Copilot</sub></li>
<li><strong>Agent</strong> -- hand it tools and let it run the whole task itself.<br>　<sub>built on <a href="https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode">opencode</a> · MCP · web · files · shell · skills · memory</sub></li>
<li><strong>Cookbook</strong> -- Scans your hardware, recommends models, click to download and serve.. easy!<br>　<sub>built on <a href="https://github.com/AlexsJones/llmfit">llmfit</a> · VRAM-aware · GGUF / FP8 / AWQ · fit scoring · vLLM / llama.cpp serving</sub></li>
<li><strong>Deep Research</strong> -- multi-step runs that gather, read, and synthesize sources into a nice visual report.<br>　<sub>adapted from <a href="https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/DeepResearch">Tongyi DeepResearch</a></sub></li>
<li><strong>Compare</strong> -- a fun tool to compare models side by side. Test completely blind, no bias!<br>　<sub>multi-model · blind test · synthesis</sub></li>
<li><strong>Documents</strong> -- YOU write the text, AI is there to assist, not the opposite.<br>　<sub>multi-tab editor · markdown · HTML · CSV · syntax highlighting · AI edits · suggestions</sub></li>
<li><strong>Memory / Skills</strong> -- Persistent memory and skills, your agent evolves over time as it better understands you and your tasks!<br>　<sub>ChromaDB · fastembed (ONNX) · vector + keyword retrieval · import/export</sub></li>
<li><strong>Email</strong> -- IMAP/SMTP inbox with AI triage built in: urgency reminders, auto-tag, auto-summary, auto-reply drafts, auto-spam.<br>　<sub>IMAP · SMTP · per-account routing · CalDAV-aware</sub></li>
<li><strong>Notes & Tasks</strong> -- Quick notes with reminders, a todo list, and scheduled tasks the agent can act on.<br>　<sub>note pings · checklist · cron-style tasks · ntfy / browser / email channels</sub></li>
<li><strong>Calendar</strong> -- Local-first calendar with CalDAV sync to Radicale / Nextcloud / Apple / Fastmail.<br>　<sub>CalDAV pull · .ics import/export · per-calendar colors · agent-aware</sub></li>
<li><strong>Works on mobile</strong> -- looks and runs great on your phone, not just desktop.<br>　<sub>responsive · installable (PWA) · touch gestures</sub></li>
<li><strong>Extras</strong> -- more to explore, happy if you give it a go!<br>　<sub>image editor · theme editor · file uploads (vision + PDF) · web search · presets · sessions · 2FA</sub></li>
</ul>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Quick Start</h2><a id="user-content-quick-start" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Quick Start" href="#quick-start"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Defaults work out of the box: clone, run, then configure models/search/email
inside <strong>Settings</strong>. Only edit <code>.env</code> for deployment-level overrides like
<code>APP_BIND</code>, <code>APP_PORT</code>, <code>AUTH_ENABLED</code>, <code>DATABASE_URL</code>, or a pre-seeded admin password.</p>
<p dir="auto">On first setup, Odysseus creates an admin account (<code>admin</code> unless
<code>ODYSSEUS_ADMIN_USER</code> is set) and prints a temporary password in the terminal.
For Docker installs, the same line is in <code>docker compose logs odysseus</code>.
Use that for the first login, then change it in <strong>Settings</strong>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Contributing? See <a href="/pewdiepie-archdaemon/odysseus/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a> for setup, testing, and
pull request guidelines.</p>

<summary>Cookbook, GPU, Ollama, and troubleshooting notes</summary>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Docker bundled services.</strong> Compose starts Odysseus, ChromaDB, SearXNG, and
ntfy. Odysseus and the bundled service ports bind to <code>127.0.0.1</code> by default, so
they are reachable from the host but not exposed to your LAN/public internet
unless you opt in.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Cookbook storage in Docker.</strong> Downloads live in <code>./data/huggingface</code>
(<code>~/.cache/huggingface</code> in the container). Cookbook-installed Python CLIs and
serve engines live in <code>./data/local</code> (<code>~/.local</code> in the container), so they
survive container recreation.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Remote servers.</strong> In <strong>Cookbook -> Settings -> Servers</strong>, generate the
Odysseus SSH key and add the public key to the remote server's
<code>~/.ssh/authorized_keys</code>. From the host you can also run:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre>ssh-copy-id -i data/ssh/id_ed25519.pub user@server</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto"><strong>Docker GPU overlays.</strong> CPU-only users can skip this section. Cookbook can
only detect GPUs that Docker exposes to the container — if the host runtime or
device passthrough is not configured, Cookbook sees the iGPU, another card, or
CPU instead of your intended GPU.</p>
<p dir="auto">For NVIDIA, <code>scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh</code> diagnoses GPU passthrough and can
optionally install the host runtime or update <code>.env</code>.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Read-only diagnostic (default — installs nothing, never edits .env):</span>
scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Print OS-specific install commands without running them:</span>
scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh --print-install-commands

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Install NVIDIA Container Toolkit on Ubuntu/Debian (requires sudo):</span>
scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh --install-nvidia-toolkit

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Write COMPOSE_FILE to .env (only when GPU passthrough is confirmed working):</span>
scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh --enable-nvidia-overlay

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Full assisted setup — install toolkit, then enable overlay if passthrough works:</span>
scripts/check-docker-gpu.sh --install-nvidia-toolkit --enable-nvidia-overlay</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto">Safety notes:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>The app never installs host GPU runtime automatically.</li>
<li>The app never edits <code>.env</code> automatically.</li>
<li><code>.env</code> is only modified when <code>--enable-nvidia-overlay</code> is explicitly passed,
and only after GPU passthrough succeeds. <code>--yes</code> skips prompts but does not
bypass the passthrough gate.</li>
<li><code>.env.bak.*</code> backups created by <code>--enable-nvidia-overlay</code> are ignored by
Git and the Docker build context.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">To enable manually without the script, add this to <code>.env</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre>COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml:docker/gpu.nvidia.yml</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto">For NVIDIA/AMD GPU support, also read the comments in the selected overlay file: docker/gpu.nvidia.yml or docker/gpu.amd.yml.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Stack-management UIs (Portainer, Coolify, Dockhand, etc.).</strong> These tools
often accept only a single Compose file and do not reliably honor <code>COMPOSE_FILE</code>
or multiple <code>-f</code> overlays. CLI users should keep using the <code>COMPOSE_FILE</code>
overlay workflow above. For stack UIs, point the stack at one of the standalone
files instead, which bundle the base stack plus the GPU settings:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>docker-compose.gpu-nvidia.yml</code> — still requires the NVIDIA Container Toolkit
on the host.</li>
<li><code>docker-compose.gpu-amd.yml</code> — still requires host ROCm/kfd/DRI setup, the
<code>video</code>/<code>render</code> group membership, and <code>RENDER_GID</code> when needed.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">The base <code>docker-compose.yml</code> plus the <code>docker/gpu.*.yml</code> overlays remain the
source of truth; the standalone files mirror them for single-file deployments.</p>

<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>GPU passthrough ≠ llama.cpp CUDA.</strong> <code>nvidia-smi</code> passing inside the
container confirms Docker GPU access, but llama.cpp also needs <code>cudart</code> and
the CUDA Toolkit at runtime. If Cookbook logs show <code>Unable to find cudart library</code>, <code>Could NOT find CUDAToolkit</code>, <code>CUDA Toolkit not found</code>, or
tensors/layers assigned to CPU, that is a Cookbook/llama.cpp build issue —
not a Docker passthrough failure. Re-install the serve engine via
<strong>Cookbook → Dependencies</strong> to get a CUDA-enabled build.</p>
<p dir="auto">The same split applies to AMD/ROCm: seeing <code>/dev/kfd</code> and <code>/dev/dri</code> inside
the container confirms device passthrough, not ROCm userspace or a
ROCm-enabled vLLM/llama.cpp build. <code>rocm-smi</code> and <code>rocminfo</code> are not expected
inside the slim Odysseus image.</p>
</blockquote>

<p dir="auto">This connects Odysseus in Docker to an Ollama server that is already running on
your host machine; it does not start Ollama inside the container.
<code>host.docker.internal</code> is Docker's hostname for the host machine from inside the
container. Cookbook <strong>Serve</strong> is a separate workflow for serving downloaded
models through Odysseus/llama.cpp, so Windows users with an existing Ollama
install usually only need to add the endpoint in Settings.</p>

<p dir="auto"><strong>Requirements:</strong> Python 3.11+. The core app (chat, agent, memory, documents,
email, calendar, deep research) runs fully native. For full <strong>Cookbook</strong> background
model downloads and the agent shell tool, also install
<a href="https://git-scm.com/download/win" rel="nofollow">Git for Windows</a> (provides <code>bash.exe</code>).
Local GPU <em>serving</em> of vLLM/SGLang needs Linux/WSL2; for a local model on Windows,

<code>http://localhost:11434/v1</code> in Settings.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Security Notes</h2><a id="user-content-security-notes" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Security Notes" href="#security-notes"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Odysseus is a self-hosted workspace with powerful local tools: shell access, file uploads, model downloads, web research, email/calendar integrations, and API tokens. Treat it like an admin console.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Keep <code>AUTH_ENABLED=true</code> for any network-accessible deployment.</li>
<li>Keep <code>LOCALHOST_BYPASS=false</code> outside local development.</li>
<li>Use <code>SECURE_COOKIES=true</code> when Odysseus is served through HTTPS by a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.</li>
<li>Do not expose it directly to the public internet without HTTPS and a trusted reverse proxy or private access layer.</li>
<li>Keep <code>.env</code>, <code>data/</code>, <code>logs/</code>, databases, uploads, generated media, backups, auth/session files, API keys, and model/provider tokens out of Git and private shares. They are ignored by default.</li>
<li>Review <code>data/auth.json</code> after first boot: disable open signup unless you intentionally want it, make only your own account admin, and keep demo/test accounts non-admin.</li>
<li>Non-admin users do not get shell/Python/file read/write by default, and admin-only routes/tools such as MCP management, API tokens, webhooks, model/cookbook serving, backup/vault, and app settings are admin-gated. Other features are controlled by per-user privileges, so review each user's privileges before exposing a deployment.</li>
<li>Rotate any API keys or tokens that were ever pasted into a shared chat, demo, screenshot, or log.</li>
<li>If you enable API tokens or webhooks, create separate tokens per integration and delete unused ones.</li>
<li>Prefer binding manual development runs to <code>127.0.0.1</code>; bind to <code>0.0.0.0</code> only when you intentionally want LAN/reverse-proxy access.</li>
<li>Keep ChromaDB, SearXNG, ntfy, Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp, databases, and raw model/provider APIs internal-only. Expose only the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint through your trusted proxy or private access layer.</li>
<li>Before publishing a fork, run <code>git status --short</code> and confirm no private files from <code>.env</code>, <code>data/</code>, <code>logs/</code>, uploads, backups, or local databases are staged.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Private or proxied deployments</h3><a id="user-content-private-or-proxied-deployments" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Private or proxied deployments" href="#private-or-proxied-deployments"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Odysseus serves plain HTTP on its app port. Docker Compose binds Odysseus and the bundled services to <code>127.0.0.1</code> by default, so a typical production/private setup is:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Keep Odysseus on localhost, for example <code>127.0.0.1:7000</code>.</li>
<li>Terminate HTTPS at a trusted reverse proxy or private access gateway.</li>
<li>Put the authenticated Odysseus web/API entrypoint behind that layer.</li>
<li>Keep raw service and model ports internal-only.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Cloudflare Access, Tailscale, Caddy, nginx, and Traefik can all fit this pattern; none are required by Odysseus. If your access layer reaches Odysseus on the same host, proxy to <code>http://127.0.0.1:7000</code> and keep <code>AUTH_ENABLED=true</code>, <code>LOCALHOST_BYPASS=false</code>, and <code>SECURE_COOKIES=true</code>.</p>

<p dir="auto">Most setup is done inside the app with <code>/setup</code> or <strong>Settings</strong>. Use <code>.env</code>
for deployment-level defaults and secrets you want present before first boot.
Key settings:</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Built-in MCP servers (optional setup)</h3><a id="user-content-built-in-mcp-servers-optional-setup" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Built-in MCP servers (optional setup)" href="#built-in-mcp-servers-optional-setup"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Odysseus auto-registers a few built-in MCP servers at startup. The npx-based ones (currently the browser server, <code>@playwright/mcp</code>) only start when their npm package is already in the local npx cache. If a package isn't cached, that server is skipped with a startup log message explaining what to do, so a fresh install does not block on a multi-minute npm download or hang if Playwright system deps are missing.</p>
<p dir="auto">To enable the browser MCP (page navigation, screenshots, vision), run once:</p>
